one_line_intent: Turn off Message Signalled Interrupts for the whole system when certain chipsets are detected.
generated_by: claude-opus-5-5 (in-session, same prompt contract as reason.py)

architecture_rationale.claim: Chipset controls buses Linux may not know about, so per-bus flags are insufficient; MSI is disabled globally.

evidence.excerpt: Instead of setting the flag on all buses in the machine, simply disable MSI globally.

intentional_vs_accidental.claim: System-wide scope is deliberate and accepted as low cost.

evidence.excerpt: Given the track record and considering the rather minimal impact of MSI, disabling it seems reasonable.

hardware_timing_dependencies.claim: VIA VT3351/VT3336/VT3364, ATI RS400/RS480, ServerWorks, SiS 761: 2000s-era chipsets whose APIC mis-handles MSI.

evidence.excerpt: The Via VT3351 APIC does not play well with MSI and unleashes a flood of APIC errors when MSI is used to deliver interrupts.

suspected_workarounds.claim: Chipset-level workaround; in K8M800 case root cause (host bridge vs AHCI) was never determined.

evidence.excerpt: it's unclear whether the culprit is with the ahci controller or the host bridge.

external_interfaces.claim: Calls pci_no_msi(): global state read by the MSI core for every device and driver.

compatibility_certification_sensitive.claim: Any device driver that assumes MSI availability silently falls back to legacy INTx on these systems.

reasoning.claim: Without it: machine hangs or interrupt floods (BCM5906, X11 start).

evidence.excerpt: Broadcom BCM5906 Ethernet controllers set up via MSI cause the machine to hang.

historical_lessons.claim: An early attempt to disable MSI per-bridge did not work because the device matched was a host controller, not a bridge; the global approach replaced it.

evidence.excerpt: doesn't work because the host controller is being quirked not a PCI bridge.
